candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans for 27 new homes on vacant land in Rochdale town centre have been approved. Great Places Housing Group applied to Rochdale Council to create a development of 27 affordable dwellings, including a three-storey apartment building containing 23 apartments, and a 2.5-storey terrace of four family homes on the land at 206-208 Drake Street. The site, on the corner of Drake Street and Broadfield Stile and which backs on to the Grade II-registered Broadfield Park, is a former DVLA test centre which has been demolished and vacant for several years. Planning permission was previously granted on appeal to build 17 homes on the site but the scheme did not materialise. The site became overgrown and a target for fly-tippers before the council bought it via compulsory purchase to ensure redevelopment could go ahead. Supporting documents by Paddock Johnson architects state: “The scheme is proposed as 100% affordable housing for social rent, providing a mix of apartment accommodation and larger family homes within a sustainable urban location. “Its redevelopment for residential use would make effective use of an underused urban site in a sustainable location, with good access to local services, public transport, green infrastructure and town centre facilities. “The scheme provides 100% affordable housing for social rent, exceeding local policy requirements, responding to an identified housing need within Rochdale and providing a substantial public benefit. candidates.source_summary: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has teamed up with new fitness centre Gymbound in a special partnership for the 2027 and 2028 seasons.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has teamed up with new fitness centre Gymbound in a special partnership for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. Gymbound will become the club’s official club-wide main shirt sponsor, with its branding set to feature on the front of playing shirts across every section of the club, from its youngest players through to its senior teams as Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its historic 70th anniversary in 2028. The agreement will also see Gymbound, in Eagle Technology Park, Queensway, support Rochdale Mayfield’s open-age pre-season training programme, providing players with access to a modern fitness environment to help improve strength, conditioning, fitness and overall preparation ahead of the new season. The partnership will introduce exclusive membership opportunities for Rochdale Mayfield players and club members, encouraging greater participation in physical activity and making fitness more accessible. Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC founder Carl Abraham said: “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Gymbound on board as our club-wide main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. “This is a significant partnership for Rochdale Mayfield and another major step forward in our ambition to become the best amateur sports club in the borough. “As a club, we are constantly looking to build relationships with local businesses that share our values, ambitions and commitment to the community. Gymbound is a fantastic example of that. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our open-age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Home » News » Member Success Story: Steven’s Incredible 15-Stone Transformation “I feel fitter, stronger and far more confident. Simple things like being able to buy clothes from normal high street shops or walk around on holiday without a T shirt are things I would never have felt comfortable doing before.” When Steven joined Heywood Sports Village, everyday activities had become a challenge. Simple tasks such as walking upstairs, tying shoelaces, travelling, and even playing with his children, were becoming increasingly difficult. At his heaviest weight, Steven felt his health and lifestyle were preventing him from fully enjoying family life. The turning point came after seeing his wife achieve her own remarkable health transformation and realising, during a family holiday, how much his weight was limiting the experiences he could share with his children. Determined to make a change, Steven committed to taking control of his health and wellbeing. Although already a member of Heywood Sports Village, Steven admits he lacked the knowledge and confidence to train effectively. Working alongside Personal Trainer Alex, gave him the skills, guidance and accountability needed to achieve lasting results. Through structured training, nutritional support and regular encouragement, Steven gradually transformed both his body and mindset. Like any significant journey, there were challenges along the way. Steven learned that progress is not always shown straight away, and there were occasions when motivation dipped and results stalled. However, the ongoing support, combined with the encouragement of his family, helped him stay focused on his long-term goals and continue moving forward. Today, Steven has lost an incredible 15 stone , completely transforming his quality of life. He now feels fitter, stronger and more confident than ever before. Activities that once seemed impossible, from everyday movement to family holidays, are now enjoyed with ease. Beyond the physical transformation, Steven says the greatest change has been the confidence gained from setting a challenging goal and proving to himself that he could achieve it. Steven’s advice to those who want to start their fitness journey: “Do not try to change everything at once. Start with smatt changes and build on them, getting little wins each day and week. Set yourself a personal goal and give yourself a clear target to work towards. Ask for support as well. The gym has a great community and people genuinely want to see each other do well. If you can, work With a coach like Alex, having someone to guide your training and nutrition and hold you accountable can make a massive difference.”

candidates.source_summary: Fifteen people have been arrested as police tackle a "spider web of criminality" in Heywood and Rochdale.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Seventeen people have been arrested as police tackle a “spider web of criminality” in Heywood and Rochdale. This morning, 250 officers carried out a series of raids as part of Operation Rivercrest which is targeting an organised crime group. The operation led to the execution of 20 warrants – mostly in Rochdale and Heywood – as well as in areas across Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside and Yorkshire. Those arrested range in age from 19 to 49. Sixteen men have been arrested on suspicion of various offences, including drugs supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery. One woman, aged 21, was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of drugs. DS Hannah Taala, of Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division, said officers focused on the crime group after violence in Heywood earlier in the year . She said: “There was a large disorder in April, where multiple people were involved in violence in the Heywood area. “It ended in some quiet serious injuries, assaults, a stab wound, using vehicles in that disorder, weapons, machetes. candidates.source_summary: Regeneration of Middleton has moved a step closer after the town was identified as a mayoral development area by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Regeneration of Middleton has moved a step closer after the town was identified as a mayoral development area by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig. Following a six-week public consultation, a report was submitted to a meeting of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) last month when the proposed designation was approved and subsequently endorsed by Rochdale Council. The Mayor notified the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government of the designation. The Secretary of State will, by Order, establish a Mayoral development corporation for the Area. The name to be given to the Mayoral development corporation is the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation. Designating the town as a mayoral development corporation is expected to help speed up furthering economic development and regeneration in Middleton. The GMCA said: “The area presents a significant opportunity to improve Middleton town centre and its surrounding communities. “Establishing the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation will help attract public and private investment, bring forward new development and support the delivery of around 1,500 new homes, including affordable homes. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A shorter than usual match preview looking ahead to the League Two home clash against Rochdale. John Brady - under pressure Setting the scene If we leave aside Vale's performance in the Football League Trophy game against Manchester City, then the worry for Jon Brady is the club's position of 23rd in League Two. There are some mitigating circumstances, as the Valiants do have games in hand, but for fans expecting the club to at the very least be contenders for promotion, this is completely unacceptable. As a result, Brady's future at the club is the subject of some debate and he can obviously help himself with better League results. This game, against opponents who are also struggling, represents a good chance to put three points on the board. Onel Hernandez - Port Vale Who could feature? Following the sideshow of the Trophy game, it's back to the real business and it seems manager Jon Brady has some crucial decisions to make - with the overall priority to bring some goal threat into the side. So, the focus is on the attack. It's tricky to know which of the forwards should get a start considering how limited Vale have been upfront. If we were to have a guess we'd go for Onel Hernandez (for his potential to create a chance) and Keyrol Figueroa (for his potential overall). But really, it's anyone's guess. In terms of injuries, Connor Hall and Ben Garrity are set to miss out while Matty Craig is out for the season. Devante Rodney Meet the visitors There's a trio of players who will be well known to Vale fans in the Rochdale ranks. Former Vale loan striker Dejaune Brown joined Dale in the summer and has two goals so far. Meanwhile, Devante Rodney has been with the club since 2022 and now has 47 goals from 151 appearances. Finally, there is midfielder Luke Hannant who joined in 2026. The visitors are on a run of poor League form as they are without a win in their last four games. That run includes a 5-0 home loss to Accrington at the weekend. They stand in seventeenth place in the table. Ben Garrity Previous meetings The two sides have met sixty times overall and it's dead level with 24 wins apiece plus twelve draws. The first meeting took place in 1929 and finished in a 3-3 draw. The last time the two sides met was in February 2022 when it finished in a 1-1 draw at Spotland. Midfielder Ben Garrity was on the mark for the Valiants. The last League game at Vale Park was in teh same season when it finished as a 2-3 defeat for Vale with Jamie Proctor scoring a brace. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Mayfield has secured a two-year sponsorship deal with Gymbound covering every team at the club, alongside pre-season training support and membership opportunities for players and members. The new Rochdale fitness facility will become Mayfield’s main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, with its branding appearing on playing shirts from the youngest age groups through to the senior sides. The agreement takes the club into its 70th anniversary year in 2028. Mayfield said its playing kit programme for both seasons is now fully sponsored. candidates.source_summary: Completion of base build marks next phase for Rochdale’s advanced materials and manufacturing innovation hub 30,000 sq. ft centre designed to connect research, specialist facilities and commercial production Development forecast to generate £107m in economic value over 10 years The base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale has been completed, marking a major milestone in the development of Atom Valley’s advanced materials and manufacturing innovation district. Designed by Bond Bryan, the 30,000 sq. ft centre will provide a physical gateway into the UK’s advanced materials and manufacturing network, connecting businesses with specialist space, facilities, research expertise and support to help move new technologies from concept towards commercial application. The building is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub in Rochdale intended to bring together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners. The next phase will focus on specialist fit-out ahead of the centre becoming operational in 2027. The project addresses a key challenge for advanced manufacturing: creating environments that support the transition from research and development to commercialisation and production, while accommodating specialist processes and allowing for emerging technologies and changing business needs. Mark Adey, director at Bond Bryan, said: “The SMMC is about creating the infrastructure that allows innovation to move beyond the laboratory and into commercialisation and manufacture. That transition places very different demands on a building, so the challenge is creating highly technical environments that work for specialist processes today, while remaining flexible enough to respond to technologies and businesses that are still emerging. “We’ve spent decades designing research, science and advanced manufacturing environments across the UK, and that experience has shown us that the most successful places connect people, ideas and processes rather than treating research and production as separate worlds. SMMC brings those elements together in one place, creating an adaptable environment that can evolve alongside the industries it supports.” Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) has led the physical development of the centre, working with the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners to secure investment and establish advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The project builds on the establishment of the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Convened by RDA, CEAMS connects businesses with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, the National Physical Laboratory (NPL), the Centre for Process Innovation (CPI) and NCC, formerly the National Composites Centre.

candidates.source_summary: Foster carers who have between them clocked up a total of 465 years supporting children and young people across the borough have been recognised by Rochdale Council.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Foster carers who have between them clocked up a total of 465 years supporting children and young people across the borough have been recognised by Rochdale Council. A total of 34 fostering families were honoured at the council’s recent annual Foster Carer Celebration Awards at Rochdale Town Hall in gratitude for their outstanding commitment to providing safe, stable and nurturing homes for some of the most vulnerable. Between all the carers, it is estimated they have supported more than 1,020 children and young people from newborn to 18, while working with the local authority. Among those celebrating their individual milestones was Michael, aged 79, and Marilyn, aged 75, who are marking 50 years. Predominantly caring for newborn babies and siblings since 1976, the married couple from Milnrow have cared for more than 330 children in that time and are still welcoming youngsters into their home. Marilyn said: “We’ve been to their weddings, adoption parties, christenings, 18th and 21st birthday parties. “It’s lovely when you think you started off with them as a baby and now, they’ve grown. Ian and Carole McLean celebrate 40 years of fostering with Rochdale Council “We’ve had letters from adoptive parents saying, ‘They’ve turned out like they have because of you’ which is nice.”

Despite having been unbeaten in the league, Sunderland were coming off the back of a very disappointing performance and defeat at home to Portsmouth just three days earlier. Luke O’Nien had been sent off late on and was suspended for this game. Phil Parkinson made changes to the line-up as a result and started with a back three of Tom Flanagan, Bailey Wright and Dion Sanderson, with Wright being the only survivor from the Pompey game. Lee Burge continued in goal behind a midfield of Denver Hume, George Dobson, Max Power and Conor McLaughlin, and a front three of Charlie Wyke, Chris Maguire and Lynden Gooch. Despite the defeat to Portsmouth, hopes were high. Sunderland hadn’t dropped a point against Rochdale in their four previous encounters, and the Lads were odds-on at the bookies. Rochdale started the game well and had the best of the opening 10 minutes. Oliver Rathbone had a deflected shot that fortunately fell for Burge, but despite this, first blood went to Sunderland, and we were ahead after only 15 minutes.
